turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Starting resistance welding electrode qualification diagnostic procedure.

ground_truth.node_text: Start

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Please complete the initial electrode inspection. Check the electrode cap faces for pitting deeper than one millimeter or any mushrooming. Examine the cap shank contact surface for corrosion or mechanical damage, and inspect the coolant port on each electrode arm for blockage.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Inspect electrode cap faces for pitting deeper than 1 mm or mushrooming. 2. Check the cap shank contact surface for corrosion or mechanical damage. 3. Inspect the coolant port on each electrode arm for blockage.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Inspection complete. The electrode caps show some minor surface wear but no pitting deeper than one millimeter, no mushrooming, and the coolant ports are clear.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Inspect electrode cap faces for pitting deeper than 1 mm or mushrooming. 2. Check the cap shank contact surface for corrosion or mechanical damage. 3. Inspect the coolant port on each electrode arm for blockage.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Are the electrode caps showing damage, severe pitting, mushrooming, or cracking?

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode cap damage, severe pitting, mushrooming or cracking?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: The electrode caps look okay, but I'm seeing significant discoloration and what looks like copper oxidation on the shank itself where it threads into the holder.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the caps are in acceptable condition with only minor wear marks. No severe damage observed.

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode cap damage, severe pitting, mushrooming or cracking?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the electrode face diameter within the wear limit?

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode face diameter within wear limit?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, I've checked the measurements and the electrode face diameter is still within the acceptable wear limit for this electrode type.

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode face diameter within wear limit?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the cooling water flow rate above minimum at both electrodes?

ground_truth.node_text: Cooling water flow rate above minimum at both electrodes?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, I've measured the flow rate at both electrodes and both are reading above the minimum specification.

ground_truth.node_text: Cooling water flow rate above minimum at both electrodes?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the electrode force within plus or minus five percent of the programmed schedule value?

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode force within ±5% of programmed schedule value?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the measured force is reading about eight percent below the programmed value. It's outside the tolerance band.

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode force within ±5% of programmed schedule value?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the pneumatic pressure regulator on the electrode arm to bring the force back into specification.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust pneumatic pressure regulator on electrode arm

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Regulator adjustment complete. I've increased the pressure setting to compensate for the low force reading.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust pneumatic pressure regulator on electrode arm

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Reverify the electrode force after the regulator adjustment.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify electrode force after regulator adjustment

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Force is now reading within tolerance. The adjustment brought it back to within three percent of the programmed value.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify electrode force after regulator adjustment

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the measured weld current within plus or minus three percent of the scheduled value?

ground_truth.node_text: Measured weld current within ±3% of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, the weld current reading from the Rogowski coil is within two percent of the scheduled value. Well within tolerance.

ground_truth.node_text: Measured weld current within ±3% of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the weld time within plus or minus one cycle of the scheduled value?

ground_truth.node_text: Weld time within ±1 cycle of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: The weld time looks fine, but I'm seeing the secondary transformer coil temperature spiking to 180 degrees even though the cooling pump is running—that's not one of the options here.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the measured weld time is off by about two cycles. The contactor is staying closed longer than programmed.

ground_truth.node_text: Weld time within ±1 cycle of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the weld timer setting in the controller schedule to correct the timing deviation.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust weld timer setting in controller schedule

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Timer adjustment complete. I've corrected the weld time parameter in the controller.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust weld timer setting in controller schedule

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Clean both electrode faces and place a sheet of carbon transfer paper between them. Close the electrodes at twenty-five percent of programmed force, then open and inspect the contact pattern on each face.

ground_truth.node_text: Clean both electrode faces and place a sheet of carbon transfer paper between them. Close the electrodes at 25% of the programmed force setting and open. Inspect the carbon transfer pattern on each face; the contact impression should be concentric and cover the full electrode face area uniformly. An off centre or crescent shaped pattern indicates electrode misalignment requiring mechanical correction.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Carbon transfer test complete. I can see the contact impression on both faces.

ground_truth.node_text: Clean both electrode faces and place a sheet of carbon transfer paper between them. Close the electrodes at 25% of the programmed force setting and open. Inspect the carbon transfer pattern on each face; the contact impression should be concentric and cover the full electrode face area uniformly. An off centre or crescent shaped pattern indicates electrode misalignment requiring mechanical correction.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Are the electrode faces parallel with the contact pattern covering above ninety percent of the face area?

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode faces parallel, contact pattern above 90% of face area?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the pattern is off-center and only covering about seventy percent of the face. The electrodes are not properly aligned.

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode faces parallel, contact pattern above 90% of face area?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the electrode arm tilt to achieve parallel contact between the electrode faces.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust electrode arm tilt to achieve parallel contact

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Alignment adjustment complete. I've corrected the arm tilt and the electrodes should now be parallel.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust electrode arm tilt to achieve parallel contact

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Prepare five test specimens from the production material stack with the correct number of layers and thickness. Weld each specimen at nominal schedule settings, label them, and measure the weld nugget diameter before proceeding to non-destructive testing.

ground_truth.node_text: Prepare five test specimens cut from the production material stack with the correct number of layers and thickness. Weld each specimen at the nominal schedule settings and label each with the weld number and machine setting used. Measure the weld nugget diameter visually or by ultrasonic means and record the result in the pilot weld log before proceeding to non destructive testing.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Hey, before I continue with this, do we need to fill out a hot work permit for using the welding equipment in this area, or is that only required in the fabrication shop?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: All five pilot welds are complete and labeled. I've recorded the nugget diameter measurements in the pilot weld log.

ground_truth.node_text: Prepare five test specimens cut from the production material stack with the correct number of layers and thickness. Weld each specimen at the nominal schedule settings and label each with the weld number and machine setting used. Measure the weld nugget diameter visually or by ultrasonic means and record the result in the pilot weld log before proceeding to non destructive testing.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Do the pilot welds show acceptable appearance with no spatter, expulsion, or surface cracks?

ground_truth.node_text: Pilot weld appearance, no spatter, expulsion or surface cracks?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: The weld looks okay visually, but I'm noticing some discoloration and oxidation around the heat-affected zone that seems unusual.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, I'm seeing some minor spatter around the weld zone on three of the five specimens. The appearance isn't quite right.

ground_truth.node_text: Pilot weld appearance, no spatter, expulsion or surface cracks?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the weld schedule by modifying the current and force parameters for this material batch.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust weld schedule, modify current and force for material batch

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Schedule adjustment complete. I've reduced the current slightly and increased the force to eliminate the spatter issue.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust weld schedule, modify current and force for material batch

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Apply ultrasonic couplant to each pilot weld coupon and scan the weld zone using an A-scan ultrasonic probe. Record the signal amplitude and back wall echo attenuation, identify the nugget boundary, and measure the nugget diameter.

ground_truth.node_text: Apply ultrasonic couplant to the electrode face side of each pilot weld coupon and scan the weld zone using an A scan ultrasonic probe. Record the reflected signal amplitude and the back wall echo attenuation. Identify the nugget boundary and measure the nugget diameter from the scan image. Compare against the minimum nugget diameter in the weld quality specification.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Hey, I'm seeing the ultrasonic probe's transducer crystal is cracked and giving erratic readings—this isn't covered in the procedure but I can't get reliable amplitude data with it damaged like this.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Ultrasonic inspection complete on all five coupons. I've recorded the measurements and compared them against the quality specification.

ground_truth.node_text: Apply ultrasonic couplant to the electrode face side of each pilot weld coupon and scan the weld zone using an A scan ultrasonic probe. Record the reflected signal amplitude and the back wall echo attenuation. Identify the nugget boundary and measure the nugget diameter from the scan image. Compare against the minimum nugget diameter in the weld quality specification.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Does the weld nugget diameter meet the minimum requirement for this material thickness?

ground_truth.node_text: Weld nugget diameter meets minimum for material thickness?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the nugget diameter is consistently undersized across all five test specimens. The measurements are falling below the minimum specification.

ground_truth.node_text: Weld nugget diameter meets minimum for material thickness?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: This procedure must be escalated. The weld nugget is undersized and requires weld engineer review. Please notify the engineering team and place this machine on production hold pending further investigation.

ground_truth.node_text: End, Escalate: nugget undersize, weld engineer review required

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Understood. I'll contact the weld engineer immediately and tag the machine as out of service.

ground_truth.node_text: End, Escalate: nugget undersize, weld engineer review required
